reporter_interpretations.text: Observation — The new frozen screening result records symmetric progressive-stiffness behavior under plus_x and minus_x. At forces 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 N, material displacement was respectively 0.007075934433888733, 0.013372461773263027 and 0.021025520057311314 m for plus_x, with effectively identical minus_x values. The corresponding interval stiffnesses were 7.940885079198062 and 13.066671687113084 N/m, giving a stiffness ratio of 1.645493110250711 against a lower bound of 1.5. Slack-to-taut transitions passed in both directions: tendon_3 engaged for plus_x and tendon_1 for minus_x, each reaching a minimum high-window tension of about 0.508404 N. The measured displacement, residual, stiffness-ratio and no-contact constraints passed in both conditions, but this is diagnostic screening rather than task acceptance.

Evidence — The proposed mechanism is supported locally by direction-specific tendon engagement and rising secant stiffness, but the dynamic records do not establish a qualified mechanism certificate. In both load directions, the low window failed tip-speed, monitor-speed and static-balance gates: plus_x values were 0.0038460496049106604 m/s, 0.003650332796072127 m/s and 0.00033820341011112174 N·m, versus limits of 0.001 m/s, 0.001 m/s and 0.00001 N·m. Recovery failures were larger: tip speed 0.009804709396080033 m/s, monitor speed 0.009305759901226396 m/s and static balance 0.0008590015838925277 N·m. This supports ongoing dynamic motion as an explanation for failed qualification. It does not identify its physical cause, and incomplete static-balance calibration remains a confounder. Static equilibrium itself was qualified at the unloaded point, so unloaded static infeasibility is weakened as an explanation.

Unresolved — Overall task success remains unknown because paired-mechanism evidence is unmeasured for both load conditions, the complete qualification grid is unavailable, and independent Replay and original acceptance were not evaluated. Consequently, signed task gap, ranking eligibility, strict parameter effects and improvement are undefined. The four saved parameter combinations are not comparable as complete tasks; their small component changes cannot establish causal superiority or interaction. Route checks found no issue at 160001 checked poses for each of eight condition-record combinations, but this certifies only those checked routes and does not replace dynamic qualification or independent acceptance evidence.
